bank.name: Computer Science
bank.subject: General Science & Ability
bank.description: Computer basics, hardware, software, storage units, the internet and modern technology.

questions.prompt: Who is regarded as the father of the computer?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, the first general-purpose computer concept.

questions.prompt: CPU stands for?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the brain of the computer.

questions.prompt: RAM is a type of?
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents when the power is off, so it is volatile.

questions.prompt: ROM is described as?
questions.explanation: Read-only memory keeps data even without power.

questions.prompt: The smallest unit of data in computing is the?
questions.explanation: A bit is the smallest unit, holding a 0 or 1.

questions.prompt: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explanation: One byte equals 8 bits.

questions.prompt: One kilobyte (KB) equals?
Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard feeds data into the computer.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: A monitor displays output from the computer.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a storage device?
questions.explanation: The hard disk stores data permanently.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Windows, Linux, macOS and Android are operating systems.

questions.prompt: MS Word is an example of?
questions.explanation: MS Word is a word processor.

questions.prompt: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW in 1989.

questions.prompt: Web pages are written in?
questions.explanation: HTML structures content on web pages.

questions.prompt: A computer virus is?
questions.explanation: A virus is malware that replicates and harms systems.

questions.prompt: Wi-Fi stands for?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is a wireless networking technology.

questions.prompt: The Windows operating system is developed by?
questions.explanation: Microsoft develops Windows.

questions.prompt: iPhone and macOS are products of which company?
questions.explanation: Apple makes iPhone, iPad and macOS.

questions.prompt: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to?
questions.explanation: AI enables machines to perform tasks that need human-like intelligence.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a search engine?
questions.explanation: Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo are search engines.

questions.prompt: Email was first used on which network?
questions.explanation: Email originated on ARPANET in the 1970s.

questions.prompt: Cloud computing means?
options: Storing and accessing data over the internet
questions.explanation: Cloud services provide storage and computing over the internet.

questions.prompt: The first electronic general-purpose computer was?
questions.explanation: ENIAC (1945) is considered the first electronic general-purpose computer.

questions.prompt: Which storage device is volatile (loses data when powered off)?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory; ROM, hard disks and SSDs retain data.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is word processing software?
questions.explanation: MS Word is used to create and edit text documents.

questions.prompt: In binary, the number 2 is represented as:
questions.explanation: Binary uses only 0 and 1; decimal 2 is written as 10 in binary.

questions.prompt: Which unit measures computer memory?
questions.explanation: Memory is measured in bytes (KB, MB, GB); hertz measures speed.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a web browser?
questions.explanation: Firefox is a browser; Windows/Linux are OSes, Android a mobile OS.

questions.prompt: What is the function of an IP address?
options: To uniquely identify a device on a network
questions.explanation: An IP address uniquely identifies a device connected to the internet or a network.

questions.prompt: Which language is directly understood by a computer's CPU?
questions.explanation: Machine language (binary 0s and 1s) is the only code a CPU executes directly.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is cloud storage?
questions.explanation: Google Drive stores files on remote servers accessible via the internet.

questions.prompt: What does 'Wi-Fi' primarily use to transmit data?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi transmits data using radio waves in the 2.4/5 GHz bands.

questions.prompt: Which part of a computer performs arithmetic and logic operations?
questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) inside the CPU handles calculations and logic.

questions.prompt: Which device is known as the brain of the computer?
questions.explanation: The CPU processes instructions and is the computer's brain.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a pointing device?
questions.explanation: A mouse is a pointing device used to move the cursor.

questions.prompt: Which operating system is developed by Apple for Mac computers?
questions.explanation: macOS is the operating system used on Apple Mac computers.

questions.prompt: Which company developed the Android operating system?
questions.explanation: Google developed Android.

questions.prompt: What does 'URL' stand for?
questions.explanation: URL identifies a resource on the web.

questions.prompt: Which language is used to create web pages?
questions.explanation: HTML structures web pages.

questions.prompt: The process of booting a computer refers to:
questions.explanation: Booting is the startup process of a computer.

questions.prompt: Which device converts digital signals to analog for internet?
questions.explanation: A modem modulates and demodulates signals.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of application software?
questions.explanation: MS Word is an application, not system software.

questions.prompt: The term 'Cloud' in computing refers to:
questions.explanation: Cloud computing delivers services over the internet.

questions.prompt: Which file format is used for compressed archives?
questions.explanation: ZIP is a compressed archive format.

questions.prompt: What does 'AI' stand for in computer science?
questions.explanation: AI is Artificial Intelligence.

questions.prompt: Which key deletes the character to the left of the cursor?
questions.explanation: Backspace removes the character on the left.

questions.prompt: A 'bug' in programming refers to:
questions.explanation: A bug is an error or flaw in software.

questions.prompt: Which part of the computer stores data permanently?
questions.explanation: The hard disk stores data permanently.

questions.prompt: Which is the most widely used operating system for personal computers?
questions.explanation: Windows dominates the desktop OS market.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of an antivirus?
questions.explanation: Antivirus software detects and removes malware.

questions.prompt: The shortcut Ctrl + Z is used to:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is a programming language; HTML is markup.

questions.prompt: The 'server' in a network is a computer that:
questions.explanation: Servers provide resources and services to clients.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a social media platform?
questions.explanation: Facebook is a social media platform.

questions.prompt: What does 'USB' stand for?
questions.explanation: USB is Universal Serial Bus.

questions.prompt: Which device is used to input text and characters into a computer?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is the primary text input device.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used to print documents on paper?
questions.explanation: A printer produces a hard copy of documents on paper.

questions.prompt: The main circuit board of a computer is called the:
questions.explanation: The motherboard connects all internal components.

questions.prompt: Which software manages hardware and provides a platform for applications?
questions.explanation: The OS, e.g. Windows or Android, manages resources.

questions.prompt: Which unit is used to measure processor speed?
questions.explanation: CPU speed is measured in gigahertz (GHz).

questions.prompt: The shortcut Ctrl+C is used to:
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C copies the selected content.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages on the internet?
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) serves web pages.

questions.prompt: Which storage device has no moving parts?
questions.explanation: Solid-state drives use flash memory and have no moving parts.

questions.prompt: A gigabyte (GB) is equal to how many megabytes (MB)?
questions.explanation: 1 GB = 1024 MB in binary computing.

questions.prompt: Which company operates the Bing search engine?
questions.explanation: Bing is Microsoft's web search engine.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a type of computer memory?
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device, not memory.

questions.prompt: Which device connects a computer to the internet via a telephone line?
questions.explanation: A modem modulates and demodulates signals.

questions.prompt: Which symbol is used to separate a file name from its extension?
questions.explanation: The dot separates name and extension, e.g. report.pdf.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to the physical parts of a computer?
questions.explanation: Hardware includes physical components like the CPU and keyboard.

questions.prompt: Which shortcut key is used to save a file?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+S saves the current document.

questions.prompt: Which type of software converts high-level code into machine language?
questions.explanation: A compiler translates source code into executable code.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used for wireless internet connection?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi transmits data wirelessly over radio waves.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a database management system?
questions.explanation: MySQL is a relational database management system.

questions.prompt: Which unit is used to measure screen resolution?
questions.explanation: Resolution is expressed in pixels, e.g. 1920×1080.

questions.prompt: Which language is used to style web pages?
questions.explanation: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls web page appearance.

questions.prompt: Which device is used to convert printed documents into digital form?
questions.explanation: A scanner digitises documents and images.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a spreadsheet program?
questions.explanation: Excel is used for data tables and calculations.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a portable storage device?
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive is a small, portable storage device.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of malware?
questions.explanation: A Trojan is malicious software that disguises itself.

questions.prompt: Which device routes data packets between networks?
questions.explanation: A router forwards packets between different networks.

questions.prompt: Which component stores frequently used data for faster access by the CPU?
questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, fast memory that sits close to the CPU.

questions.prompt: What does RAM stand for?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) temporarily stores data for the running programs.

questions.prompt: Which key locks all typed letters in capital form when pressed once?
questions.explanation: Caps Lock toggles the case of typed letters until it is pressed again.

questions.prompt: Which software is used to send and receive email?
questions.explanation: An email client such as Outlook or Gmail manages sending and receiving mail.

questions.prompt: Which file extension indicates a Word document?
questions.explanation: .docx is the standard extension for Microsoft Word documents.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to receive email from a mail server?
questions.explanation: POP3 and IMAP retrieve email from the server to the client.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a markup language?
questions.explanation: HTML is a markup language; the others are programming languages.

questions.prompt: The file extension for a web page is usually:
questions.explanation: Web pages usually use the .html (or .htm) file extension.

questions.prompt: The 'www' stands for:
questions.explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an email service?
questions.explanation: Gmail is an email service; Photoshop is image software and Chrome is a browser.

questions.prompt: A network that connects computers within a single building is a:
questions.explanation: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a single building or campus.

questions.prompt: Which file extension is used for executable files in Windows?
questions.explanation: Windows executable files have the .exe extension.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a type of printer?
questions.explanation: Laser and inkjet printers are common types of printers.

questions.prompt: Which key combination is used to switch between open windows?
questions.explanation: Alt + Tab switches between open windows in Windows.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a free and open-source operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is a free and open-source operating system.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to send email?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send email.

questions.prompt: Which unit is commonly used to measure printer speed?
questions.explanation: Printer speed is measured in pages per minute (ppm).

questions.prompt: Which icon stores deleted files before permanent removal in Windows?
questions.explanation: The Recycle Bin temporarily stores deleted files before permanent removal.

questions.prompt: Which language is used to add interactivity to web pages?
questions.explanation: JavaScript adds interactivity to web pages, while HTML provides structure.

questions.prompt: Which sorting algorithm has an average time complexity of O(n log n)?
questions.explanation: Merge sort (and quicksort) have an average time complexity of O(n log n).

questions.prompt: The full form of PDF is?
questions.explanation: PDF stands for Portable Document Format, developed by Adobe.

questions.prompt: Which device works as both an input and an output device?
questions.explanation: A touchscreen displays output and also accepts touch input.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used to connect a computer to a high-definition TV?
questions.explanation: HDMI carries high-definition audio and video over a single cable.

questions.prompt: Which chip of a computer is responsible for rendering graphics?
questions.explanation: The graphics processing unit (GPU) renders images, video and animations.

questions.prompt: The full form of LAN is?
questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network, which covers a small area such as an office.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to browse web pages securely?
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts web traffic between the browser and the server.

questions.prompt: The shortcut key to select all text in a document is?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+A selects the whole document or all items in the current view.

questions.prompt: Which type of memory is used in USB flash drives?
questions.explanation: Flash memory is non-volatile and retains data without power, making it ideal for USB drives.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not an input device?
questions.explanation: A printer produces output on paper; the others feed data into the computer.

questions.prompt: Which device converts analog signals into digital signals for a computer?
questions.explanation: An ADC samples analog signals such as sound and converts them to digital values.

questions.prompt: The full form of GPS is?
questions.explanation: GPS stands for Global Positioning System, used for location and navigation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a wearable computing device?
questions.explanation: A smartwatch is worn on the wrist and functions as a portable computer.

questions.prompt: The full form of JPEG is?
questions.explanation: JPEG is a standard image compression format named after its committee.

questions.prompt: Which key is commonly used to refresh a web page?
questions.explanation: F5 reloads the current page in most web browsers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an image editing software?
questions.explanation: Adobe Photoshop is a professional image editing program.

questions.prompt: The standard layout of keys on an English keyboard is called?
questions.explanation: Most English keyboards use the QWERTY layout, named after its first six letter keys.

questions.prompt: Which unit is commonly used to measure internet connection speed?
questions.explanation: Internet speed is measured in megabits per second (Mbps).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a network topology?
questions.explanation: Star is a common network topology in which all nodes connect to a central hub or switch.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a mobile operating system?
questions.explanation: Android is a Linux-based operating system designed for smartphones and tablets.

questions.prompt: The full form of ISP is?
questions.explanation: An ISP supplies internet access to homes and businesses.

questions.prompt: Which component of a computer supplies power to all other components?
questions.explanation: The power supply unit (PSU) converts mains electricity into the voltages the computer needs.

questions.prompt: Which key deletes the character to the right of the cursor?
questions.explanation: Delete removes the character after the cursor; Backspace removes the one before it.

questions.prompt: Which type of cable is used for very high speed internet connections?
questions.explanation: Fibre optic cables carry data as light pulses at very high speeds.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a graphics file format?
questions.explanation: PNG is a lossless raster image format widely used on the web.

questions.prompt: Which application is used to create slide presentations?
questions.explanation: PowerPoint is the standard tool for making slide presentations.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an antivirus program?
questions.explanation: Norton Antivirus protects a computer by detecting and removing malware.

questions.prompt: Which key combination switches between open tabs in a web browser?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Tab moves between browser tabs; Alt+Tab switches between open windows.

questions.prompt: Which program is used to compress and decompress files?
questions.explanation: WinRAR creates and extracts compressed archives such as ZIP and RAR files.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a spreadsheet file extension?
questions.explanation: .xlsx is the file extension of Microsoft Excel workbooks.

questions.prompt: Which operating system is used on iPhones?
questions.explanation: iOS is the operating system that powers iPhones and iPads.
